name: Alabama
fails: Confusing Alabama's 30-day free look period (replacement policies) with the standard 10-day period
Missing questions on Alabama's life insurance replacement regulations (specific disclosure forms required)
Underestimating the state law section — 17% of L&H questions are Alabama-specific
law: Alabama requires agents to complete a 20-hour pre-licensing course approved by the Alabama Department of Insurance. The course must include specific modules on Alabama insurance law and ethics.
tip: The Pearson VUE interface uses a 'mark and review' feature. Use it aggressively — mark uncertain questions and come back. The 2.5-hour limit is generous; most students finish with time to spare.

name: Alaska
apply: Alaska Division of Insurance within 180 days
fails: Alaska's surplus lines regulations — unique rules for placing coverage with non-admitted insurers
Variable product licensing — requires FINRA securities registration in addition to state license
Mixing up Alaska's continuing education requirements with pre-licensing requirements
law: Alaska requires agents to provide a Notice Regarding Replacement whenever a new policy may cause an existing one to lapse or be surrendered. This signed form must be retained by the agent.
tip: PSI exams in Alaska follow the same format nationwide. The state-specific law section (20%) is where many students drop points. Focus extra study time on the Alaska Division of Insurance's official regulations.

name: Arizona
apply: NIPR.com; license issued within 2–3 business days
fails: Arizona's Community Property rules and how they affect beneficiary designations
Distinction between admitted vs. non-admitted insurers in Arizona
Arizona's unclaimed property laws as they relate to life insurance proceeds
law: Arizona is a community property state. Assets acquired during marriage are jointly owned, which can affect insurance policy ownership and beneficiary designations. Spouse's consent may be required.
tip: Pearson VUE centers are in Phoenix, Tucson, and Flagstaff. Book early — centers fill up in Phoenix. Exam scoring is immediate; you'll know your result before leaving the testing center.

name: Arkansas
fails: Arkansas's replacement regulations — very specific disclosure requirements
Long-term care partnership program rules unique to Arkansas
The Arkansas Insurance Code sections on unfair claims practices
law: Arkansas participates in the Long-Term Care Partnership Program, allowing policyholders to protect assets equal to their LTC benefits paid from Medicaid spend-down requirements.
tip: The state law section weighs 17% of the exam — don't underestimate it. Study directly from the Arkansas Insurance Department's official exam content outline, which lists specific statutes tested.

name: California
hours: 12 hours (Code & Ethics only — AB 943, eff. Jan 1, 2026)
fails: California's extensive state law section (30%) — the largest of any state
California-specific ethics requirements — anti-fraud and unfair competition rules heavily tested
FAIR Plan — California's insurer of last resort for high-risk properties including fire zones
law: Per AB 943 (effective January 1, 2026), California eliminated the 20-hour line-specific prelicensing requirement. Only the 12-hour Code & Ethics course is required. The California Insurance Code has strict rules around life settlement regulations and the California Life and Health Insurance Guarantee Association (CLHIGA).
tip: California's 30% state law weight means you're essentially studying two exams. The CDI publishes a detailed exam outline — use it as your study checklist. Many students fail because they underweight the California-specific material.

name: Colorado
apply: NIPR.com; Colorado Division of Insurance processes within 3–5 days
fails: Colorado's hailstorm-related property claims procedures
Managed care regulations specific to Colorado's insurance market
Senior protection laws around the sale of annuities to elderly clients
law: Colorado has strong senior protection regulations — agents must follow specific suitability standards when selling annuities or life insurance to seniors (65+), including documenting financial situation.
tip: Colorado exams are in Denver, Colorado Springs, and Fort Collins. Bring two forms of ID — a government-issued photo ID and a secondary ID.

name: Connecticut
fails: Connecticut's 40-hour pre-licensing requirement — students often underestimate the course depth
Connecticut's mandatory managed care regulations — specific requirements for HMOs and PPOs
Surplus lines tax requirements unique to Connecticut
law: Connecticut requires 40 hours of pre-licensing education — double the national norm. The Connecticut Insurance Department is one of the more rigorous regulators in the country.
tip: PSI provides an official candidate handbook for Connecticut. Download it and review the content outline page by page. Connecticut's state law section is heavier than average — plan for it.

name: Delaware
apply: Delaware Department of Insurance via NIPR.com
fails: Delaware's insurance holding company regulations — DE is a major corporate domicile
Surplus lines licensing provisions specific to Delaware
Delaware's specific replacement and disclosure rules for life insurance
law: Delaware is home to hundreds of insurance companies due to its corporate-friendly laws. The exam tests specific rules about insurance holding company systems — groups of companies under common ownership or control.
tip: Delaware's exam covers 25% state law — higher than average. If you have a background in corporate law or finance, the holding company regulations will feel familiar.

name: Florida
apply: FL DFS MyProfile portal; fingerprinting required
fails: Florida's 27% state law section — the state has uniquely complex insurance regulations
Florida No-Fault (PIP) auto insurance — specific personal injury protection rules
Citizens Property Insurance Corporation — Florida's insurer of last resort for homeowners
law: Florida has a 40-hour pre-licensing requirement and a large state law section (27%). Florida also has unique health insurance mandates including specific continuation of coverage rules and strong consumer protections that go beyond federal COBRA requirements.
tip: Florida's exam has 160 questions — 10 more than most states. The 40-hour pre-licensing requirement must include specific Florida law content. Practice answering questions quickly; time can be a factor here.

name: Georgia
apply: Georgia Office of Insurance via NIPR.com
fails: Georgia's 40-hour requirement — students rush the pre-licensing course and arrive underprepared
Georgia FAIR Plan provisions for high-risk properties
Replacement regulations specific to Georgia
law: Georgia requires a specific Notice to Applicant form whenever an agent replaces an existing life insurance policy. This form must be signed by the applicant and retained by the agent.
tip: Pearson VUE centers are in Atlanta, Augusta, Savannah, and Macon. Schedule at least 2 weeks out in Atlanta. Complete your 40-hour course from an approved provider; Georgia audits records.

name: Hawaii
fails: Hawaii's mandatory employer health insurance law — unique in the nation
Hawaii's HIPA (Prepaid Health Care Act) rules
Understanding Hawaii's no-fault auto insurance requirements
law: Hawaii is the only state with a mandatory employer health care law (the Prepaid Health Care Act). Employers must provide health coverage to employees working 20+ hours per week.
tip: Hawaii's PSI exam centers are in Honolulu. If you're on a neighbor island, you'll need to travel to Oahu (or use approved remote proctoring if available). Plan travel and accommodations well in advance.

name: Idaho
apply: Idaho Department of Insurance via NIPR.com
fails: Idaho's surplus lines regulations
Workers' compensation provisions — Idaho has a state-run fund alongside private insurers
Idaho-specific crop insurance provisions (agriculture is a major industry)
law: Idaho has a State Insurance Fund for workers' compensation — a public entity that competes with private insurers. Agents need to understand the role of the State Insurance Fund.
tip: Idaho's exam is straightforward compared to coastal states. The state law section focuses on standard NAIC model law applications. Thorough study of universal concepts will carry you far.

name: Illinois
apply: Illinois Department of Insurance via NIPR.com
fails: Illinois's 28% state law section — higher weighting than most states
Illinois Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Association rules
Variable annuity regulations specific to Illinois
law: Illinois has detailed regulations around life insurance replacement — agents must complete a Replacement Notice and provide specific disclosures. Illinois also has strong rules about rebating and twisting.
tip: Illinois PSI centers are in Chicago, Springfield, and Rockford. Book Chicago centers at least 2 weeks out. Exam scores are reported immediately upon submission.

name: Indiana
apply: Indiana Department of Insurance via NIPR.com
fails: Indiana's unfair claims settlement practices specific provisions
Senior-specific annuity suitability rules
Indiana's producer licensing reciprocity agreements
law: Indiana has specific producer licensing requirements including a background check for all new applicants. Felony convictions can disqualify an applicant.
tip: Students who fail Indiana often cite the state law section. Study the Indiana Insurance Code's producer licensing and unfair practices sections closely — these are the highest-frequency test topics.

name: Iowa
fails: Iowa's crop insurance provisions — major agricultural state
Iowa Life and Health Guarantee Association rules
Continuing education requirements for post-licensing
law: Iowa is a major agricultural state and includes questions about crop insurance and multi-peril crop insurance (MPCI). These federally-backed programs through the USDA Risk Management Agency are unique to agricultural states.
tip: Don't skip the crop insurance material. Iowa examiners include it specifically because it's unique to the state's market. A few crop insurance questions can be the difference between passing and failing at 70%.

name: Kansas
fails: Tornado/windstorm specific property coverage provisions — Kansas is in Tornado Alley
Kansas automobile liability laws including required minimums
Medicare Supplement (Medigap) regulations in Kansas
law: Kansas has specific windstorm deductible requirements for property policies. Because Kansas sits in Tornado Alley, insurers may apply separate higher deductibles for windstorm losses.
tip: PSI centers in Kansas are in Wichita, Topeka, and Overland Park. Wichita centers book up quickly. Book 1–2 weeks in advance.

name: Kentucky
apply: Kentucky Department of Insurance via NIPR.com
fails: Kentucky's insurance fraud statutes — more detailed than many states
Workers' compensation in Kentucky — unique system structure
Life settlement regulations specific to Kentucky
law: Kentucky's Commissioner of Insurance has broad authority to regulate market conduct. The exam tests specific enforcement provisions — what triggers a market conduct examination, what penalties apply.
tip: Focus extra study time on the state law section's enforcement and penalties provisions — these are frequently tested and students often underestimate the level of specificity required.

name: Louisiana
apply: Louisiana Department of Insurance via NIPR.com
fails: Louisiana's Civil Law tradition — LA operates under civil law (not common law)
Flood insurance regulations — Louisiana's Gulf Coast location makes flood coverage central
Louisiana Citizens Property Insurance Corporation rules
law: Louisiana is the only state with a legal system based on the Napoleonic Code (Civil Law) rather than English common law. This affects insurance contract interpretation and beneficiary rights.
tip: You don't need to be a legal scholar on Civil Law. Know that Louisiana's legal tradition is different and that this can affect policy interpretation — especially around beneficiary rights and community property.

name: Maine
apply: Maine Bureau of Insurance via NIPR.com
fails: Maine's individual health insurance market rules — strong consumer protections
Maine's guaranteed issue health insurance regulations
Long-term care partnership program specifics
law: Maine has strong guaranteed issue health insurance laws — insurers cannot deny individual health coverage based on health status. This pre-dates the ACA and is more expansive.
tip: Maine's health insurance market rules are more consumer-protective than most states. If a question gives you a scenario where an insurer denies an individual health policy in Maine, the answer is almost certainly that this is NOT allowed.

name: Maryland
fails: Maryland's 29% state law section — one of the highest weightings in the country
Maryland Health Connection (ACA marketplace) interaction with private insurance
Surplus lines regulations specific to Maryland
law: Maryland has the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) with strong consumer protection mandates. The exam specifically tests the Insurance Article of the Maryland Code, including the Commissioner's power to examine, fine, and revoke licenses.
tip: Maryland's 29% state law section demands serious attention. Use the MIA's official study guide as a primary reference. Students who treat the state section as secondary frequently fail Maryland's exam on the first try.

name: Massachusetts
apply: MA Division of Insurance via NIPR.com; CORI check required
fails: Massachusetts's 32% state law section — the highest state law weight in the entire country
Massachusetts auto insurance (unique system — managed competition with state-structured forms)
Chapter 176D (unfair claims settlement practices) — frequently tested in detail
law: Massachusetts has a unique automobile insurance system — historically the only state where most auto insurance rates were set by the state. Today it's managed competition, but MA still has unique auto regulations.
tip: Massachusetts's 32% state law weight means you need to treat the Massachusetts Insurance Code as a second subject entirely. Budget at least 5 extra hours specifically on MA law.

name: Michigan
fails: Michigan's no-fault auto insurance system — one of the most complex in the country
The Michigan Catastrophic Claims Association (MCCA) — unique to Michigan
Michigan's unlimited PIP option and the 2020 auto insurance reform
law: Michigan underwent a major auto insurance reform in 2020. Drivers can now choose PIP benefit levels: unlimited, $500K, $250K, $50K (Medicaid recipients), or opt-out (Medicare recipients).
tip: Michigan's 2020 auto reform is fresh material — don't use older prep books that don't cover these changes. The Michigan DIFS website has official guidance on the new PIP tiers.

name: Minnesota
fails: Minnesota's no-fault auto insurance requirements
Minnesota Life and Health Guaranty Association provisions
Senior citizen protection regulations in insurance sales
law: Minnesota is a no-fault auto insurance state. Drivers must carry PIP coverage that pays medical expenses regardless of fault. Know Minnesota's minimum PIP requirements and threshold rules.
tip: The no-fault auto system appears in multiple question formats. Understanding the verbal threshold vs. monetary threshold is a key distinction to master.

name: Mississippi
fails: Mississippi's producer licensing requirements and background check provisions
Mississippi Life and Health Guaranty Association rules and coverage limits
Replacement regulations specific to Mississippi — disclosure form requirements
law: Mississippi requires agents to complete a 20-hour pre-licensing course and pass a background check before licensure. Agents must be appointed by an insurer before transacting business on behalf of that insurer.
tip: Focus on the state law section which covers the Mississippi Insurance Department's producer licensing rules, unfair practices statutes, and continuing education requirements.

name: Missouri
fails: Missouri's unfair trade practices regulations
Annuity suitability standards specific to Missouri
Missouri Life and Health Guaranty Association rules
law: Missouri has specific annuity suitability regulations requiring agents to make documented recommendations based on the client's financial profile. Know what information must be gathered before recommending an annuity.
tip: Missouri's annuity suitability questions tend to be scenario-based. Centers are in Kansas City, St. Louis, and Springfield. Practice applying the suitability rules to real client situations.

name: Montana
fails: Montana's Workers' Compensation State Fund — Montana has a competitive state fund
Rural agricultural coverage provisions
Montana's unfair discrimination rules in underwriting
law: Montana has strong unfair discrimination laws in insurance that prohibit basing coverage decisions on certain protected characteristics. Know what Montana specifically prohibits insurers from using as a rating factor.
tip: PSI has limited centers in Montana — Billings, Great Falls, and Missoula. Rural applicants should plan travel accordingly. Schedule at least 2–3 weeks ahead.

name: Nebraska
fails: Nebraska's crop insurance provisions — major agricultural state
Nebraska's Life Settlement Act — regulations governing life policy sales to investors
Continuing education requirements post-licensure
law: Nebraska has a Life Settlement Act that regulates the sale of life insurance policies on the secondary market. Know the definition of a life settlement, who needs to be licensed, and disclosure requirements.
tip: Nebraska and Iowa share similar agricultural insurance themes. Nebraska's Pearson VUE center is primarily in Omaha.

name: Nevada
apply: Nevada Division of Insurance via NIPR.com
fails: Nevada's continuing education ethics requirement — unique mandatory ethics hours
Senior-specific annuity suitability standards
Nevada's anti-rebating provisions
law: Nevada has strict rules about annuity suitability for seniors. Agents must complete a one-time 8-hour training course on senior suitability before selling annuities to clients age 65+.
tip: Nevada's exam is held in Las Vegas, Reno, and Henderson. Las Vegas centers book very quickly — schedule at least 2 weeks out. The senior annuity suitability content is Nevada-specific and worth focused study time.

name: New Hampshire
apply: New Hampshire Insurance Department via NIPR.com
fails: New Hampshire's 40-hour pre-licensing requirement
Unique auto insurance provisions — NH is one of only two states that doesn't require auto insurance
Workers' compensation exemptions for small employers
law: New Hampshire is one of only two states in the U.S. that doesn't mandate auto liability insurance. Drivers may legally drive without insurance but are personally liable for any damages they cause.
tip: The auto insurance exemption is the most memorable and tested NH-specific fact. No other state has this exact provision.

name: New Jersey
fails: New Jersey's no-fault PIP auto insurance — one of the more complex no-fault systems
New Jersey's individual health insurance market regulations — strong consumer protections
FAIR Plan and JUA (Joint Underwriting Association) for hard-to-insure properties
law: New Jersey has strong individual health insurance market regulations including guaranteed issue and community rating requirements. Insurers in New Jersey cannot deny individual health coverage based on health status.
tip: Map out NJ's two lawsuit options clearly in your notes. Scenario questions will describe a driver and ask which option is in effect based on the described coverage situation.

name: New Mexico
fails: New Mexico's community property rules and insurance implications
New Mexico's Workers' Compensation Act specifics
Health insurance continuation rules beyond COBRA
law: New Mexico is a community property state, meaning property acquired during marriage is jointly owned by both spouses. This affects beneficiary rights, policy ownership, and characterization of insurance proceeds.
tip: New Mexico's PSI centers are in Albuquerque and Santa Fe. The community property rules overlap with Arizona and other Western community property states.

name: New York
apply: NY DFS via NIPR.com; fingerprinting required
fails: New York's state law section (27% L&H) — one of the most heavily regulated states
New York's unique auto no-fault (PIP) system with specific mandatory benefits
NY Insurance Law Article 54 — life settlements and viatical settlements
law: New York is one of the most heavily regulated states for Life & Health. New York has unique health insurance mandates — insurers must cover certain benefits that other states don't require.
tip: New York requires fingerprinting and a background check before your license is issued — not before the exam. Pass first, then start the background process.

name: North Carolina
fails: FAIR Plan provisions — North Carolina has a specific program for high-risk properties
NC's beach and coastal properties — North Carolina Insurance Underwriting Association (NCIUA)
Medicare Supplement regulations specific to NC
law: The North Carolina Insurance Underwriting Association (NCIUA) — also called the Beach Plan — provides wind and hail coverage for coastal properties that private insurers won't cover.
tip: Pearson VUE centers are in Charlotte, Raleigh, Greensboro, and Wilmington. The NCIUA/Beach Plan content is NC-specific and won't appear on most other state exams.

name: North Dakota
fails: North Dakota's monopolistic state workers' comp fund (Workforce Safety & Insurance)
Crop and farm insurance provisions
ND's surplus lines regulations
law: North Dakota is one of four monopolistic workers' compensation states — all workers' comp must be purchased from the state-operated Workforce Safety & Insurance (WSI). Private workers' comp insurers cannot compete in North Dakota.
tip: The four monopolistic workers' comp states — North Dakota, Ohio, Washington, and Wyoming — are frequently tested as a group. Know all four by name. The mnemonic 'NOWW' helps lock them in.

name: Ohio
fails: Ohio's monopolistic workers' comp fund (BWC) — Bureau of Workers' Compensation
Ohio's specific annuity replacement regulations
Ohio Life and Health Guarantee Association rules
law: Ohio's Bureau of Workers' Compensation (BWC) is the state's workers' compensation fund. Ohio is a monopolistic workers' comp state — private insurers generally cannot sell workers' comp to Ohio employers.
tip: PSI centers are in Columbus, Cleveland, Cincinnati, and Toledo. Focus on Ohio's Life and Health Guarantee Association coverage limits and the specific replacement regulations.

name: Oklahoma
fails: Tornado/severe weather property coverage provisions — Oklahoma is in Tornado Alley
Oklahoma's windstorm deductible rules
The Oklahoma FAIR Plan for high-risk properties
law: Oklahoma, like Kansas, sits in Tornado Alley. Insurers in Oklahoma can apply separate wind/tornado deductibles on property policies. Know how these deductibles work and how they interact with standard policy deductibles.
tip: Oklahoma's exam content is fairly standard. The windstorm and tornado coverage provisions are the most unique elements. Study these specifically using the Oklahoma Insurance Department's producer licensing guide.

name: Oregon
fails: Oregon's rebating exception — Oregon actually allows certain forms of rebating
Oregon's auto insurance minimum requirements
Oregon's small employer health insurance regulations
law: Oregon is one of very few states with a limited rebating exception. Most states prohibit rebating entirely. In Oregon, certain premium discounts or incentives are permitted under specific conditions.
tip: If a question asks whether rebating is always illegal in Oregon — the answer is NO. Know the specific conditions under which Oregon permits limited rebating. This is Oregon's most unique exam topic.

name: Pennsylvania
fails: Pennsylvania's no-fault choice auto insurance (limited tort vs. full tort)
Pennsylvania's FAIR Plan for property coverage
State-specific health insurance continuation rules beyond COBRA
law: Pennsylvania has specific health insurance continuation rules beyond COBRA. The Pennsylvania Insurance Department requires carriers to offer continuation of group health coverage to employees and dependents who lose group coverage.
tip: Pennsylvania's 24-hour pre-licensing requirement is slightly different from the 20-hour norm. Make sure your course is approved by the Pennsylvania Insurance Department and meets the 24-hour minimum.

name: Rhode Island
fails: Rhode Island's 40-hour pre-licensing requirement
Rhode Island's health insurance market rules — small state, specific carrier regulations
RI Life and Health Guaranty Association provisions
law: Rhode Island requires 40 hours of pre-licensing education and has specific continuing education requirements (24 hours every 2 years including 3 hours of ethics). The Rhode Island Insurance Division regulates both the market and agent conduct closely.
tip: Rhode Island's PSI center is in Providence — the only testing location in the state. Book well in advance. The exam follows PSI's standard interface.

name: South Carolina
fails: SC Wind Pool — South Carolina Wind and Hail Underwriting Association for coastal properties
Senior protection regulations around annuity sales
SC's unfair trade practices statute specifics
law: The South Carolina Wind and Hail Underwriting Association (SC Wind Pool) provides coverage for properties in coastal counties that private insurers won't write.
tip: Coastal wind coverage pools are tested in every coastal state — SC Wind Pool for SC, NCIUA for NC, Louisiana Citizens for Louisiana, TWIA for Texas, MWUA for Mississippi. Learning the concept once helps you apply it state by state.

name: South Dakota
fails: Trust-owned life insurance (TOLI) — South Dakota is a major trust domicile
South Dakota's surplus lines regulations
Credit insurance regulations unique to South Dakota
law: South Dakota is one of the most popular trust domicile states. This creates a unique market for trust-owned life insurance (TOLI) — life policies owned by irrevocable life insurance trusts (ILITs).
tip: South Dakota's exam includes questions about insurance trust structures you won't see in most other states. 3–5 questions can make the difference. Review TOLI and irrevocable trust basics before your exam.

name: Tennessee
fails: Tennessee's free look period — 10 days for most policies but 30 days for Medicare Supplement
TennCare — Tennessee's Medicaid program and its interaction with private insurance
Tennessee Life and Health Guaranty Association limits
law: TennCare is Tennessee's Medicaid managed care program. Tennessee contracts with private managed care organizations to deliver Medicaid benefits. Agents need to understand how TennCare interacts with private coverage.
tip: Tennessee's TennCare/Medicaid interaction questions are specific to TN but follow standard coordination of benefits logic. If you understand general Medicaid coordination rules, Tennessee's questions won't surprise you.

name: Texas
fails: Texas's 28–30% state law section — huge and very specific
Texas Workers' Compensation opt-out — Texas is the ONLY state where employers can legally opt out
Texas Windstorm Insurance Association (TWIA) for Gulf Coast properties
law: Texas is the only state in the country where employers can legally opt out of workers' compensation. 'Non-subscriber' employers choose not to carry workers' comp but lose certain legal protections and can face civil lawsuits from injured employees.
tip: Texas has Pearson VUE centers in every major city. The 40-hour pre-licensing and 28–30% state law weight make Texas one of the more demanding exams. The workers' comp opt-out is THE most Texas-specific exam topic — know it cold.

name: Utah
fails: Utah's insurance fraud statutes — strict enforcement with civil and criminal penalties
Medicare Supplement standardized plan rules
Utah's continuing education requirements post-license
law: Utah has strong insurance fraud statutes with specific civil and criminal penalties. Know the difference between civil fraud (insurance fraud as a tort) and criminal fraud (a felony under Utah law).
tip: Utah's PSI centers are in Salt Lake City and Provo. The fraud statutes section is tested specifically in Utah — review the Utah Insurance Fraud Act's definitions and penalties.

name: Vermont
fails: Vermont's single-payer health care history — VT was the first state to pass a single-payer law (later repealed)
Vermont Captive Insurance regulations — Vermont is the #1 captive insurance domicile in the U.S.
Small employer health insurance market rules specific to Vermont
law: Vermont is the #1 captive insurance domicile in the United States. A captive insurance company is a closely held insurer whose primary purpose is to insure the risks of its owner(s).
tip: The captive insurance concept is unique to Vermont in the licensing exam context. Most students don't study it — which means those who do have an advantage.

name: Virginia
apply: Bureau of Insurance (VA SCC) via NIPR.com
fails: Virginia's auto insurance alternative — VA allows a 'pay-to-not-insure' annual fee option
Virginia Life, Accident & Sickness Insurance Guaranty Association specifics
Virginia's surplus lines regulations
law: Virginia allows drivers to pay an annual uninsured motor vehicle fee to the DMV instead of carrying liability insurance. This is NOT insurance — it allows uninsured driving but doesn't protect the driver from financial liability.
tip: Virginia's Pearson VUE centers are in Richmond, Norfolk, Northern Virginia, and Roanoke. Virginia and New Hampshire are the only two states with this type of provision — know both.

name: Washington
fails: Washington's monopolistic workers' comp fund (L&I — Department of Labor & Industries)
Washington State's Long-Term Care insurance mandate (WA Cares Fund) — unique in the U.S.
Washington's auto insurance minimum requirements
law: Washington is a monopolistic workers' comp state AND passed the WA Cares Fund — the nation's first mandatory state long-term care program (2021). Washington employees pay a payroll tax (0.58% of wages) and can receive LTC benefits after a vesting period.
tip: The WA Cares Fund is a nationally unique exam topic. Washington agents must understand how the state LTC mandate works, who is exempt, and how it interacts with private LTC insurance.

name: Washington D.C.
fails: D.C.'s unique jurisdiction status — not a state, governed by unique laws
D.C.'s mandatory health insurance provisions — D.C. has its own individual mandate
D.C. workers' compensation system — operates differently from surrounding states
law: Washington D.C. has its own individual health insurance mandate requiring residents to maintain qualifying health coverage. D.C. enacted its own mandate after the federal ACA individual mandate penalty was reduced to $0 in 2019.
tip: D.C.'s exam is administered by Pearson VUE centers serving the Northern Virginia/Maryland area. The D.C. individual mandate is the most distinctive local law element.

name: West Virginia
fails: WV's competitive state workers' comp history (BrickStreet/Encova Insurance privatization)
Mining and extraction industry insurance provisions
WVOIC consumer protection regulations
law: West Virginia privatized its workers' compensation system in 2008, moving from a monopolistic state fund to a private market. WV is NO LONGER a monopolistic workers' comp state — private insurers compete freely.
tip: The workers' comp privatization is the most important historical change for West Virginia's exam. Students often assume WV has a state monopoly like OH, ND, WA, and WY. It doesn't — this is a common and costly trap.

name: Wisconsin
fails: Wisconsin's community property rules — WI is one of only nine community property states
Wisconsin's insurance small claims court process
Continuing education post-license requirements
law: Wisconsin is one of nine community property states. The Wisconsin Marital Property Act governs joint ownership of marital assets, which affects insurance beneficiary designations and policy ownership.
tip: Memorize all nine community property states: Arizona, California, Idaho, Louisiana, Nevada, New Mexico, Texas, Washington, and Wisconsin. Mnemonic: 'All Cars Idling Loudly Need New Tires Will Work.'

name: Wyoming
fails: Wyoming's monopolistic workers' comp fund (Wyoming Workers' Compensation Division)
Oil and gas industry insurance provisions
Wyoming's specific surplus lines tax requirements
law: Wyoming is one of four monopolistic workers' compensation states — all workers' comp coverage must go through the state-operated Wyoming Workers' Compensation Division. Private workers' comp insurers cannot compete in Wyoming.
tip: PSI centers are in Cheyenne and Casper. Book 2–3 weeks ahead. Wyoming's exam is straightforward otherwise — focus heavily on the monopolistic workers' comp concept and standard universal concepts. The NOWW mnemonic covers Wyoming perfectly.
